column3: A five-story tower above the Yangtze, made famous by a Tang poem about a yellow crane. It has been rebuilt many times and gives a wide view of Wuhan.
One of the biggest city lakes in China, with long walking paths, cherry and plum gardens and boats on the water.
The first bridge to span the Yangtze, opened in 1957, with a road deck above and a railway below.
A lane lined with stalls and shops that sell Wuhan's breakfast and snacks, including hot dry noodles and bean-skin pancakes.
The museum holds the chime bells of Marquis Yi of Zeng, about 2,400 years old, which can still play music.
A campus famous for its cherry blossoms in spring and its old buildings with green tiled roofs on a hillside.
Wuhan's favorite breakfast noodles are tossed with sesame paste, soy sauce, pickles and scallions. They are eaten dry, not in soup.
A thin pancake of tofu skin wrapped around sticky rice, meat and mushrooms, and pan-fried to a golden crisp.
A freshwater bream steamed whole and served with ginger and scallions. Mao Zedong praised it in a poem.
A comforting soup of pork ribs simmered for hours with crumbly lotus root, a Hubei home dish.
Spicy braised duck, sold in boxes across China. It started as a Wuhan street snack with a sweet-and-spicy taste.
A creamy fish soup with rice noodles, thickened with fish bones, eaten for breakfast in Hubei.
The ancient kingdom of Chu was known for its lacquerware, bronzes, silk and music, and for the poet Qu Yuan.
Han opera is an old local style of opera from Hubei, said to be one of the ancestors of Peking opera.
The largest hydropower station in the world, a 2.3-kilometer-long wall across the Yangtze. Ships go through its giant ship locks.
A scenic area in the Xiling Gorge with villages, waterfalls, and boat trips, showing the culture of the Tujia people.
The longest of the Three Gorges, with steep cliffs, shoals and a history of dangerous rapids that are now calm.
A shrine for the poet Qu Yuan, who lived in the Chu kingdom. The Dragon Boat Festival honors his memory.
A bright green river that winds between tall limestone cliffs, like a long painted scroll.
A light, bouncy fish paste, steamed and served in soup, a typical banquet dish in Yichang.
Sweet, thin-skinned tangerines grown along the Yangtze valley, picked in autumn.
The highest peak in central China, in the forest reserve of Shennongjia, home to rare plants and legends of a wild man.
Pork smoked over a wood fire in the mountain farms, deep in flavor, and cooked with vegetables in winter.
A city wall of the Ming and Qing periods that survived for hundreds of years, one of the best preserved in the south.
A museum with treasures of the Chu state and a well-preserved body from a Han tomb that still has soft skin.
A memorial garden for Guan Yu, the Three Kingdoms general, who guarded Jingzhou and is honored for his loyalty.
A soft, light steamed fish cake that is served at banquets and holidays in Jingzhou.
Eel cut into long strips and braised in a spicy sauce, a Jingzhou specialty.
An old wall on the Han River, with a moat, built to guard a strategic city in the Three Kingdoms period.
Noodles in a bold, spicy beef broth, a Xiangyang breakfast favorite served in every corner shop.
A deep canyon with cliffs and a tall stone pillar that rises from the valley, among the most scenic in central China.
One of the longest caves in China, with a huge entrance, an underground river and giant chambers.
Small, creamy potatoes from the highlands, roasted or fried with chili and cumin.
Green tea grown in soil rich in selenium, and Enshi is known as the selenium capital of China.
Soft, sweet lotus root from the lakes of Daye, often stewed in soup.
A sweet cake scented with osmanthus flowers, a popular treat in Xianning.
A Taoist mountain with temples on its peaks, famous for Wudang martial arts and for its blend of architecture and nature. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
A bronze hall at the top of Wudang Mountain, covered in gold color, high above the clouds.
A huge reservoir that supplies water to Beijing through the South-to-North Water Diversion Project.
A green tea grown on the mountain, linked to the Taoist monks who tended its bushes.
